thread:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT PAGER — P1 routing anomaly detected: spikes in 5xx + >200ms tail latency for gen endpoints in eu-west-1. Automatic regional spillover triggered to fallback pool (cpu-quantized) starting 2024-11-03T14:03:12Z. Pager: @Ava @Sam

Ava: I'm on it. seeing elevated error-rate on /v1/generate (model: open-redwood-v2) — errors are mostly TokenizationError and a few InvalidModelResponse. Customer impact: a small % of requests returned garbled text; a few customers reported timeouts.

Sam: Can you dump recent routing decisions and the router logs for a sample trace id? I'll start triage.

Ava: grabbing logs now — will paste traces with sensitive fields redacted.

Ava: ```
# router log excerpt (redacted)
2024-11-03T14:02:58Z ROUTER route_req id=trace-8f3a ... src=eu-west-1 dest=eu-west-1-pool
2024-11-03T14:03:12Z ROUTER spillover id=trace-8f3a reason=pool_overloaded dest=fallback-cpu-quantized-eu-west
2024-11-03T14:03:12Z PROXY handshake id=trace-8f3a upstream=dn-guard-v2 status=200
2024-11-03T14:03:12Z MODEL_INVOC invocation id=trace-8f3a model=open-redwood-v2-quantized status=200 tokens_out=0 error=TokenizationError
2024-11-03T14:03:14Z ROUTER route_req id=trace-9b2d ... src=eu-west-1 dest=eu-west-1-pool
2024-11-03T14:03:14Z ROUTER spillover id=trace-9b2d reason=pool_overloaded dest=fallback-cpu-quantized-eu-west
2024-11-03T14:03:14Z MODEL_INVOC invocation id=trace-9b2d model=open-redwood-v2-quantized status=500 error=InvalidModelResponse
```

Miran: initial hypothesis: the fallback selection logic selected a quantized variant (open-redwood-v2-quantized) with a different tokenizer or incompatible token vocab mapping. TokenizationError would fit that. Also the handshake shows PROXY status=200 but the model returned 0 tokens — odd. Could be mismatch in model spec metadata between router and pool.

Kevin: Uploading a snapshot of the routing policy state and model metadata for the pools involved.

Kevin: ```
# routing-policy snapshot (abridged)
route: eu-west-1 -> primary-pool: gpu-v100 (open-redwood-v2)
fallbacks:
  - fallback-cpu-quantized-eu-west (open-redwood-v2-quantized) priority=low
  - fallback-crossregion (open-redwood-v2) priority=medium
policy_version: 2024-11-02T10:22:01Z
# model-metadata for fallback-cpu-quantized-eu-west
model: open-redwood-v2-quantized
tokenizer: legacy-bpe-v1
max_seq: 2048
quantization: int8
```

Ava: Ok, tokenizer mismatch seems plausible — primary uses `unified-bpe-v2`. We should stop routing to the quantized pool until we confirmTokenizer compatibility.

oncall-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/routing-fallback — Suggested immediate mitigation: disable automatic spillover to pools with unknown tokenizer metadata OR pin fallback to regionally-matching model.

Sam: For immediate mitigation I propose: 1) disable spillover to fallback-cpu-quantized-eu-west (temp) 2) enable cross-region fallback to fallback-crossregion (same model family) 3) throttle new requests in eu-west to reduce pressure while we fix metadata. Anyone object?

ops-bot: metric snapshot: https://grafana.internal/d/routers/eu-west-1?panel=tail_latency — tail latency 95p rose from 120ms -> 760ms after 14:02Z; error-rate 5xx rose to 4.2% for a 4 minute window.

Miran: agree with Sam. Also we should collect an example payload that produced TokenizationError and run it against both tokenizers to show mapping differences. I can do that.

Kevin: I've queued a policy change: `disable_spillover(pool=fallback-cpu-quantized-eu-west)` — will apply in 30s. Rolling change with canary to avoid broad blast. Patching now.

Ava: Applying throttle rule: `rate_limit::eu-west-1::20rps` for the gen endpoints.

Kevin: Policy change applied: disabled spillover for fallback-cpu-quantized-eu-west (change-id c4d3f). Confirming router now prefers fallback-crossregion.

Ava: After the change, error-rate dropped to ~0.5% and tail-latency back to ~180ms. Customers reporting fewer degraded responses.

Sam: Good. Next: RCA notes to capture in thread: 1) Root cause: fallback selection lacked tokenizer-compatibility check; model metadata for some fallback pools had stale/incorrect tokenizer field. 2) Contributing factors: recent deployment that updated quantized pool metadata without schema validation; emergency autoscaler bump increased load and triggered spillover. 3) Detection: alerts on 5xx + tokenization errors and sudden token_out=0 in invocation logs. 4) Immediate mitigations: disable problematic fallback, fallback to cross-region pool, throttle incoming RPS. 5) Long-term fixes: add tokenizer compatibility check in routing decision, schema validation on pool metadata, and telemetry for tokenization-errors to map to pools.

Miran: I reproduced TokenizationError locally: sample prompt -> tokenizer `legacy-bpe-v1` produces unknown token ids for some tokens used by `unified-bpe-v2` mapping, causing the model runtime to error. Will attach small repro in eval harness.

Ava: Attaching repro snippet: ```python
# repro: run against two tokenizers
prompt = "Translate: Hello, world — special: ½ √"
print(tokenize(prompt, 'unified-bpe-v2'))
print(tokenize(prompt, 'legacy-bpe-v1'))
```

Sam: Action items (owners & ETA):
- Miran: add tokenizer compatibility check to router (PR + tests) — ETA 48h
- Kevin: add metadata schema enforcement to pool deploy pipeline (CI gate) — ETA 72h
- Ava: run customer impact sweep and notify top affected accounts; draft post-incident communication — ETA 4h
- SRE: create alert for sudden token_out=0 spikes mapped to pools — ETA 24h

Kevin: I'll follow up with a small postmortem document and link it here when ready.

Ava: Handoff: Sam going off shift in 20m, Kevin will take P1 after that. Sam, anything to add before you sign off?

Sam: No, all looks covered. Leaving notes in incident board. If anything regresses page Kevin. 

Kevin: Taking over. Adding timeline and logs to the incident doc.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigations applied, monitoring healthy. Will continue to track until cleanup tasks complete. :white_check_mark:

Kevin: Last note — we should also audit any automated model tagging jobs; I suspect a deploy job renamed tokenizer field key from `tokenizer` -> `tokenizer_name` in one of the quantization deploy manifests last week. That would cause the router to see an empty tokenizer string. Adding that to the postmortem checklist.

Ava: thanks everyone. I'll consolidate notes and send to #postmortems once Kevin posts the writeup.

Sam: :thumbsup:

Kevin: closing pager handoff.
